August 27, 2026

Veterans group launches multi-million dollar billboard campaign over Iran war

tags: politics, war
sources: @aaronparnas

VoteVets, the largest Democratic veterans organization in the country, has launched a multi-million dollar campaign to educate Americans about what it calls the illegal war in Iran and its impact on the cost of living. The group has put up nearly a thousand billboards across the country, concentrated near military bases in ten target states: Ohio, New York, North Carolina, Texas, Virginia, Florida, Colorado, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, and Georgia. The effort is part of the group's Iran accountability campaign, aimed at telling veterans who is responsible for the war.

CIA director's Moscow visit followed by UK warning to prepare for conflict

tags: war, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow, the first such visit since 2021, ahead of Russia's invasion of Ukraine. On returning to the United States he met with President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The United Kingdom has since told its citizens and military to prepare for potential conflict with an adversary understood to be Russia, amid concern that Russia may escalate beyond Ukraine into a NATO member state.

Backlash builds against Flock surveillance cameras as CEO calls for compromise

tags: surveillance, privacy, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The CEO of Flock is urging a national compromise over the company's surveillance cameras as communities destroy the devices and officials cancel contracts. Tempe, Arizona has cancelled all of its Flock contracts, and Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said he would act on the cameras because they abridge privacy too far. More than 120,000 Flock cameras are deployed nationwide; they are intended to help locate crime suspects and missing children, but have been misused by law enforcement officers to track partners, former spouses and other individuals.

Florida grand jury finds DeSantis administration diverted $10 million from children's health insurance

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A sealed Florida grand jury report obtained by CBS concludes that the DeSantis administration misappropriated $10 million in taxpayer money earmarked for health insurance for children in low-income communities. The funds were routed through the Hope Florida Foundation to political committees working to defeat a ballot measure legalizing marijuana. The report identifies Senator Ashley Moody, who previously served as Florida attorney general, as having knowledge of the arrangement.

RFK Jr. accused of lying under oath about Samoa vaccine trip

tags: politics, health, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Reporting by the Guardian and the Associated Press has surfaced a letter indicating Robert F. Kennedy Jr. gave false testimony during his confirmation hearing, where he said a 2019 trip to Samoa had nothing to do with vaccines. In the letter, written to the prime minister of Samoa ahead of the trip, Kennedy discusses investigating adverse health events associated with vaccines and states his belief that recent deaths linked to the MMR vaccine were a manifestation of such effects. The disclosure has prompted calls for criminal perjury charges.

Bears Ears and Grand Staircase protections cut as mining claims are filed

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Nearly three million acres across Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante have been removed from monument protection by executive order, and the Bears Ears Commission, the tribal body that helped guide management of the territory, has been dissolved. Utah Governor Spencer Cox has said removing the protections and opening the land to mining and drilling will allow people to enjoy it, though parts of Bears Ears are fenced off because of unstable and unsafe abandoned mines that have historically been cleaned up at taxpayer expense. Nine new mining claims have already been filed, ahead of the September 11 date when the land formally reopens to new claims. The affected areas include sacred sites and land that Indigenous peoples have stewarded for generations.

Sailor who went overboard from USS Abraham Lincoln faces military discipline

tags: military, health
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

A Navy sailor who jumped from the USS Abraham Lincoln in what his wife describes as a suicide attempt is now facing non-judicial punishment for violations of the Uniform Code of Military Justice. According to MSNOW, the charges include Article 83 for malingering, defined as intentionally faking an illness or injuring oneself to avoid duty, and Article 86 for absence without leave. Possible penalties include a reduction in pay. The incident has raised concerns about conditions aboard the carrier.

Pentagon review finds classified Abbey Gate documents were kept in safes

tags: military, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Pentagon investigators reviewing the Abbey Gate bombing say they found highly relevant classified documents that had been hidden away in safes. The finding comes five years after the attack during the withdrawal from Afghanistan.

Purple Heart recipients wounded in Iranian drone attack say care is still out of reach

tags: military, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

Soldiers awarded the Purple Heart after being wounded in an Iranian drone attack say they are still fighting to obtain the medical care they need. Their accounts point to continuing gaps in treatment for troops injured in the conflict.

White House social media accounts stumble through a day of errors

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The Department of Education posted a clip of Gary Oldman as Winston Churchill saying "you cannot reason with the tiger with your head in its mouth" followed by a montage of President Trump, apparently unaware the line refers to Adolf Hitler and Churchill's rejection of appeasement; the post was deleted and blamed on a staffer. The official White House account then posted an image of a bald eagle holding a goose's head in ice to suggest the United States had beaten Canada, but the source video shows the goose prevailing. The president has since posted his own material, including a map altered with a marker to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America." A separate post placed Washington, D.C. within North Carolina.

FDA recalls saline bags over possible fiberglass contamination

tags: health
sources: @aaronparnas

The FDA has issued a recall of saline bags over the potential presence of particulate matter identified as fiberglass in the saline solution. The affected product was distributed to health care providers and distributors in Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Louisiana, Maryland, Missouri, North Carolina, New Jersey, Nevada, New York, Ohio, South Carolina, Texas, and Virginia.

Researchers examine toxic blowback from firearm suppressors on troops

tags: military, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

Suppressors reduce noise and blast for troops using them, but researchers are now asking what repeated exposure to toxic blowback may be doing to service members' health. The questions center on the cumulative effects of that exposure over the course of a military career.

Navy seeks torpedo that glides through the air before hunting submarines

tags: military, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Navy wants to develop a torpedo capable of gliding through the air, entering the water and then hunting submarines. The weapon could potentially be released from altitudes as high as 60,000 feet.

Tropical Storm Dolly forms in the central Atlantic

tags: climate
sources: @aaronparnas

Tropical Storm Dolly has formed in the Atlantic Ocean and is moving westward at 24 miles per hour. The current projected track carries it toward the Caribbean, and some models show it potentially reaching Florida or the East Coast.
